title: disk-encryption on windows: BitLocker demands the recovery key after a change
scenario: On windows, a disk-encryption problem: BitLocker demands the recovery key after a change. Symptom: 'BitLocker recovery screen at boot'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'bitlocker_recovery' for disk-encryption on windows
expected_reasoning: A firmware/TPM/boot change invalidated the TPM seal, triggering recovery — this is expected, not corruption.
Unlock with the escrowed recovery key, then re-seal to the TPM so it stops prompting.
Do not disable BitLocker to avoid the prompt.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'BitLocker demands the recovery key after a change' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('bitlocker_recovery') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.
possible_mistakes: Decrypt the drive entirely to stop the prompt (loses protection).
Not knowing where the recovery key is escrowed (AD/AAD/MSA).
hints: The recovery key is escrowed in AD/Entra/Microsoft account — retrieve it there.
Re-enable the TPM protector after a legitimate firmware change to re-seal.
reference_solution: Re-seal to TPM; confirm Protection On
alternative_solution: Suspend BitLocker before a planned firmware update to avoid the prompt entirely.
edge_cases: Secure Boot toggled off is the real trigger; turning it back on restores the seal.
goal: Cifratura disco: BitLocker demands the recovery key after a change. Sblocca/ripristina il volume senza perdere dati.
